title: Gene Digital Circuits Based on CRISPR-Cas Systems and Anti-CRISPR Proteins
protocol: Design the sgRNA/crRNA expression cassette using RNA polymerase III-dependent SNR52 promoter for one-terminus cassettes.
Include the sgRNA/crRNA sequence in the designed cassette.
Add the SUP4 terminator to complete the one-terminus cassette design.
Use RNA polymerase II-dependent ADH1 promoter for another-terminus RGR11 cassettes.
Insert an RGR structure containing two ribozymes (HH and HDV) and sgRNA/crRNA sequence in-between.
Include the ADH1 terminator to complete the RGR11 cassette design.
Design spacer sequences for Cas9/Cas12a-mediated transcriptional activation.
Harness the bacterial lex operator sequence (lexOp) as the target site.
Insert the lexOp into the CYC1 promoter driving yeast-enhanced green fluorescent protein (yEGFP).
Define the spacer sequence complementary to and targeting the inserted lexOp.
Check the orthogonality of the spacer sequence using CRISPRDIRECT tool.
Paste the lexOp sequence flanked by the PAM sequence in the text field.
Define the PAM sequence as NRG for dCas9 and TTTV for dCas12a.
Specify the species from the drop-down list as Budding Yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) S288C Genome.
Click on Design.
Make sure there is no matching target site in 20mer+PAM nor in 12mer+PAM search.
Construct the sgRNA/crRNA expression cassette.

Prepare a reaction mixture containing: 20-40 ng of DNA template, 1 µL of 10 µM forward primer (i.e., ot25), 1 µL of 10 µM reverse primer (i.e., ot26), 5 µL of 2.5 mM dNTP mix, 0.5 µL of DNA polymerase, 10 µL of 5x DNA polymerase reaction buffer, and ddH2O up to a total volume of 50 µL.
Run the touchdown PCR program on a thermocycler at Stage 1: 98 °C for 30 s.
Continue with Stage 2: 98 °C for 10 s, 68 °C for 20 s, and 72 °C for 15 s, repeated for 10 cycles.
Proceed to Stage 3: 98 °C for 10 s, 59 °C for 20 s, and 72 °C for 15 s, repeated for 25 cycles.
Finish with Stage 4: 72 °C for 2 min.
Hold at 4 °C until starting the follow-up experiments.
Isolate PCR products via gel electrophoresis (100 V, 30 min).
Elute DNA sequences from the agarose gel using a DNA gel extraction kit.
Digest the shuttle vector with SacI and Acc65I at 37 °C for 1 h.
Prepare the reaction mixture by adding 5 µg of the shuttle vector, recommended amounts of enzymes, digestion buffer, and ddH2O to reach a total volume of 30 μL.
Verify the shuttle vector digestion via gel electrophoresis.
Inactivate the two enzymes at 65 °C for 20 min.
Insert purified PCR products into the cut-open shuttle vector using Gibson assembly method by incubating equimolar DNA mixture at 50 °C for 1 h.
Transform Escherichia coli DH5α competent cells with the Gibson reaction mixture via heat shock transformation.
Transfer transformed E. coli cells onto LB agar plates containing ampicillin (0.1 g/L).
Incubate plates at 37 °C overnight to grow colonies.
Pick four colonies from the LB agar plate and culture separately overnight in LB solution containing ampicillin (0.1 g/L) at 37 °C.
Extract plasmids from E. coli cells using mini-preparation procedure.
Sequence and confirm inserted transcription unit using primers ot18 and ot19 via Sanger method.
Design scaffold guide RNA (scRNA) composed of sgRNA sequence and MS2 hairpin structures.
Synthesize scRNA template to accommodate different spacer sequences for pSNR52-spacer_DR(SpCas9)-2×MS2(wt+f6)-SUP4t.
Design proper primers for PCR on necessary spacer sequences.
Construct an scRNA expression cassette according to the procedures in step 1.3.
Obtain the plasmid pTPGI_dSpCas9_VP64.
Digest the plasmid pTPGI_dSpCas9_VP64 and acceptor vector with XbaI and XhoI at 37 °C for 1 h or overnight as needed.
Separate and purify the insert fragment and acceptor vector.
Ligate the purified insert fragment and acceptor vector with T4 DNA ligase at 16 °C for 8 h.
Prepare ligation solution by adding equimolar amounts of the purified acceptor vector and target fragments, 1.5 µL of T4 buffer, 0.5 µL of T4 ligase, and ddH2O to a total volume of 15 µL.
Confirm the newly constructed plasmid is correct through digestion with XbaI and XhoI at 37 °C for 1 h followed by gel electrophoresis.
Synthesize two yeast codon-optimized dCas12a proteins (denAsCas12a and dLbCas12a) flanked by BamHI and Xhol restriction enzyme sites.
Construct the acceptor vector pRSII406-promoter-ATG-NLS-GS-HIStag-GS-BamHI-sp-XhoI-AD-NLS-TAA-mTGUO1 via touchdown PCR and Gibson assembly method.
Insert each dCas12a protein into the constructed acceptor vectors via digestion with BamHI and Xhol, then ligate them with T4 DNA ligase.

Construct an acceptor vector for galactose-inducible expression cassettes of dCas12a as pRSII406-Acc651-pGAL1-ATG-NLS-GS-HIStag-GS-BamHI-sp-XhoI-GS-NLS-TAA-CYC1 using touchdown PCR and Gibson assembly method.

Digest the plasmids containing dCas12a proteins and acceptor vector with BamHI and Xhol, then ligate them with T4 DNA ligase to get the plasmid pRSII406-pGAL1-Acc651-ATG-NLS-GS-HIStag-GS-BamHI-dCas12a-XhoI-GS-NLS-TAA-CYC1t.

Digest the obtained plasmid with Acc65I and BamHI, then replace pGAL1 with pGPD via touchdown PCR and Gibson assembly method to construct pRSII406-pGPD-ATG-NLS-GS-HIStag-GS-BamHI-dCas12a-XhoI-GS-NLS-TAA-CYC1t.
Obtain plasmids containing sequences of type II Acrs (AcrIIA2, AcrIIA4, AcrIIA5) and type V-A Acrs (AcrVA1, AcrVA4, AcrVA5).
Construct plasmids based on the pRSII403 shuttle vector to express Acrs.
Amplify four different promoters (pGPD, pACT1, pTEF2, genCYC1t_pCYC1noTATA) using touchdown PCR.
Amplify three kinds of AcrIIA and two terminators (ADH1t and CYC1t) using touchdown PCR.
Assemble a series of TUs expressing AcrIIAs under different promoters via the Gibson assembly method.
Synthesize acceptor sequence: ATG-FLAGtag-GS-BamHI-sp-XhoI-NLS-GS-NLS-TAA-Tsynth6.
Assemble acceptor vectors pRSII403-promoter-ATG-FLAGtag-GS-BamHI-sp-XhoI-NLS-GS-NLS-TAA-Tsynth6, where the promoter is: pGAL1, pTEF1, genCYC1t_pCYC1noTATA.
Assemble acceptor vectors via the Gibson assembly method.
Insert each of the three AcrVAs into the acceptor vector via touchdown PCR and the Gibson assembly method.
Extend the sequence of AcrIIA4 with the sequences of the GS linker and HBD(hER).
Obtain GS-HBD and AcrIIA4 parts separately using touchdown PCR.
Put AcrIIA4, GS-HBD, and the shuttle vector into the Gibson mixture.
Construct the complete plasmid via the Gibson method.
Culture yeast cells overnight in 2 mL of synthetic defined complete medium (SDC) using a 24-well plate at 30 °C and 240 rpm.
Dilute the cell culture (1:100) into 2 mL of fresh SDC and keep growing the yeast cells at 30 °C, 240 rpm, for another 4 h.
Harvest the whole 2 mL of the cell solution and centrifuge at 20,238 x g for 2 min.
Remove the supernatant carefully since the cell pellet is small.
Extract the RNA from yeast cells using an RNA kit.
Prepare a 1% agarose gel.
Mix 5 µL of each RNA sample with 1 µL of DNA loading dye.
Load the mixture onto the gel and run it.
Ensure clear bands at ~4,000 nt and ~2,000 nt for ribosomal RNA (25S/18S) are present on the gel.
Check for a blurred band at ~80 nt corresponding to tRNA.
Use the RNA samples immediately for cDNA synthesis or store them at -80 °C for future use.
Reverse transcribe crRNA using the stem-loop method to form the first strand of cDNA.
For sgRNA reverse transcription, follow the same procedure as for cDNA synthesis of the ACT1 gene.
Take the RNA template, primer, and buffers out of the freezer.
Let them melt on ice.
Prepare 10 μL of the reaction mixture according to the kit instructions.
Put the mixture in a thermal cycler at 42 °C for 2 min.
Transfer the mixture onto ice.

Prepare 20 µL of the reaction mixture by adding 10 µL of the previous mixture, 1 µL of stem-loop primer (2 µM concentration), 2 µL of 10x RT reaction buffer, 2 µL of reverse transcription enzyme mix, and 5 µL of RNase-free H2O.
Place the reaction mixture in a thermal cycler at 25 °C for 5 min.
Incubate the mixture at 50 °C for 15 min.
Heat the mixture to 85 °C for 5 min.
Use the product immediately or store it at -80 °C.
Prepare a 13 µL mixture consisting of the primer mix, dNTP mix, RNA template (1 μg), and RNase-free water according to the kit instructions.
Put the mixture into a thermal cycler at 70 °C for 10 min.
Prepare the reaction mixture for cDNA synthesis by adding reagents as described in the kit instructions.
Place the mixture in a thermal cycler and incubate at 50 °C for 15 min.
Incubate further at 85 °C for an additional 5 min.
Use the product immediately for qPCR or store it at -80 °C.
Prepare the qPCR reaction mixture according to the manufacturer's instructions for the SYBR kit.
Set a preincubation stage in a real-time PCR machine: 10 min at 95 °C.
Program the PCR stage to run 45 cycles, each cycle consisting of 15 s at 95 °C followed by 34 s at 55 °C.
Set the melting stage to run as follows: 10 s at 95 °C, then 60 s at 65 °C, and finally 1 s at 97 °C.
Pick some yeast cells using a sterile loop and culture them in 5 mL of YPD-rich medium overnight at 240 rpm at 30 °C.
Add 500 µL of the cell solution to 20 mL of fresh YPD and grow them at 240 rpm at 30 °C until OD600 reaches 0.6.
Mix 5 mL of the culture with 500 µL of 37% formaldehyde and let it stay at room temperature for 10 min.
Harvest the cells by centrifugation at 1,500 x g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cells with 1 mL of fixation buffer (0.1 M KH2PO4, 0.5 M MgCl2, 3.7% formaldehyde, pH = 6.5).
Keep the cell solution at room temperature for 20 min.
Centrifuge the cell solution at 1,500 x g for 5 min and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of washing buffer (0.1 M KH2PO4, 1.2 M sorbitol, pH = 6.5) supplemented with 4 µL of beta-mercaptoethanol and 4 µL of lysate solution (5 mg/mL).
Put the cell solution into an incubator at 37 °C for 20 min.
Centrifuge the cell solution at 1,500 x g for 5 min and discard the supernatant.
Wash the cell pellet twice with 1 mL of PBS by centrifugation (1,500 x g for 5 min).
Resuspend the cells in 100 µL of PBS plus 0.05% Tween 20 and add 4 µL of BSA solution (10 mg/mL).
Keep the cell solution at room temperature for 20 min.
Add the Anti-His tag primary antibody to the mixture in step 7.1.6 at a 1:400 dilution.
Incubate the solution at room temperature for 2 h.
Centrifuge the mixture at 1,500 x g for 5 min and remove the supernatant.
Add 1 mL of PBST and centrifuge (1,500 x g) for 5 min to wash the cell pellet.
Repeat this operation twice.
Discard the supernatant and suspend the cells in 100 µL of 1x PBST.
Mount the cells on a slide by taking 2 μL of the cell solution and placing it on a glass slide.
Cover the cell solution with a coverslip.
Observe the cells under a fluorescence microscope.
Turn on the fluorescent light source, microscope, and computer.
Write down the fluorescent light source number and open the microscope software on the computer.
Put the slide on the microscope stage.
Choose the 40x objective lens and observe the cells under the green light (550 nm).
Move the coarse focus knob until the contour of yeast cells appears.
Move the fine focus knob to focus the cells.
Detect the cells with the microscope software.
Close the microscope field of view and switch to the computer screen.
Click on Live, wait for 3-5 s, and click on Capture to take a picture.
Save the picture.
Turn off the computer, microscope, and fluorescent light source.
Culture yeast cells at 30 °C and 240 rpm for FACS experiments.
Grow cells containing dCas12a-VPR gene in SDC solution for 24 h.
Dilute cells containing dCas12a-VPR gene at a ratio of 1:100 in fresh SDC.
Incubate diluted cells containing dCas12a-VPR gene for another 12 h before measuring fluorescence intensity.
Grow cells modified with AcrIIA4-HBD(hER) gene overnight in SDC.
Measure OD600 of the cells after growth.
Dilute culture to OD600 = 0.1 by adding a diverse concentration of β-estradiol.
Incubate diluted cells in fresh medium for another 7 h before FACS experiments.
Switch on the FACS machine 20 min before measurements.
Mix 20 μL of cell culture with 300 μL of ddH2O for sample preparation.
Run FACS software and create a new experiment.
Set measurement parameters (FSC(SSC)-A/H/W and histogram).
Select the FITC or GFP filter for yEGFP.
Set the acquisition cell number to 10,000.
Measure the intensity of fluorescent beads with the FITC filter voltage.
Adjust the FITC filter voltage if necessary.
Wash the machine with ddH2O to remove excess beads.
Click on Preview and wait for sample injection stability.
Click on Acquire to start measuring sample fluorescence intensity.
Measure the beads again at the end of the experiment.
Check whether the relative difference in bead measurements exceeds 5%.
Export FACS data as FCS files.
Analyze FCS files with R Studio software using Flowcore package.
Open R studio and load the script Bdverse analysis.R.
Set the experiment name (ename).
Specify the directory (path) where the FCS files are stored (dir_d).
Indicate the directory (dir_r) for result file creation.
Set the fluorescence channel.
Set the number of samples measured.
Set the dimensions for dot plots.
Set the maximal length of x and y axis for bar and box plots.
Choose the gating method by removing the # from corresponding lines.
Select the flowSet object gated, corresponding to chosen gating method.
Select the dot plot resolution.
Uncomment flt_low <- filter_low(sp) to remove negative fluorescence measurements.
Uncomment flt_sp <- filter(flt_lw) to remove outliers due to other experiments.
